senses.definition: (transitive) To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.
examples: Christmas gifts are commonly known to be wrapped in paper.

quotes.text: I then dried these over a flame, and then, wrapping the formes and re-sealing them with my court seals — for my only commission, you see, was to report as to whether the type was unpied, and text ungarbled, and the formes all ready […]

senses.definition: (transitive) To enclose or coil around an object or organism, as a form of grasping.
examples: A snake wraps itself around its prey.

quotes.text: Like one who wraps the drapery of his couch / About him, and lies down to pleasant dreams.

The prehistoric caribou they had already liberated was wrapped in a space blanket and carefully tied to a sled. The Science Foundation team had then moved on to a deep translucent blue seam in the ice that proved to be a window on the rest of the ungulant herd standing poised in suspended animation, as if waiting for time to start again.

senses.definition: (transitive, figurative) To conceal by enveloping or enfolding; to hide.

quotes.text: wise poets that wrap truth in tales

senses.definition: (transitive or intransitive, video production) To finish shooting (filming) a video, television show, or movie.
examples: To avoid going over budget, let's make sure we wrap by ten. (compare wrap up 2)

senses.definition: (transitive, lines, words, text, etc.) To break a continuous line (of text) onto the next line
examples: I wrapped the text so that I wouldn't need to scroll to the right to read it.

senses.definition: (computing, transitive) To make functionality available through a software wrapper.
(transitive or intransitive) To (cause to) reset to an original value after passing a maximum.
examples: The row counter wraps back to zero when no more rows can be inserted.

senses.definition: Paper or sheeting that is wrapped around something to protect, contain, or conceal it.

subsenses.definition: (automotive) A large sheet of self-adhesive material applied over a vehicle's paintwork for decorative or protective purposes.

quotes.text: The media theorist Peter Lunenfeld[…] says illustrative art is often used to defang threatening technology. He compares the Waymo wraps to Google Doodles, which distract people while they are using a complex and opaque search engine algorithm that is “almost fully beyond our ken.”

senses.definition: A loose piece of women's clothing that one wraps around the body; a shawl or scarf.
(chiefly in the plural, now rare) An outer garment worn as protection while riding, travelling etc.

quotes.text: ‘I see you have had our Lowick Cicero here,’ she said, seating herself comfortably, throwing back her wraps, and showing a thin but well-built figure.
